info.bio: punk and D-Beat band fundada en 1979. sus tres primeros albums se convirtieron en auténticos clásicos del punk, hasta 1984. posteriormente Discharge grabó tres intentos fallidos de heavy metal con los albums: "grave new world", "massacre divine" y "shooting up the world". 2002 Discharge decidió volver a sus origenes.

scenes.name: Punk-rock británico
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: La gira de los Ramones de 1976 contagia a Inglaterra, donde el punk es combinación de moda y paro: la Gran Bretaña de Thatcher, con las ciudades industriales devastadas, convierte el «punk» en algo mucho más serio que lo que pretendían los Ramones. Malcolm McLaren inventa el sonido (Sex Pistols, «los Ramones con heroína y valium») y la imagen. The Clash, los más intelectuales (London Calling, Sandinista); Damned, Generation X, Buzzcocks (inventores del punk-pop), Vibrators. En Australia, Radio Birdman y los Saints. La segunda ola (GBH, UK Subs, Neurotics, New Model Army, Stiff Little Fingers) y el punk anarquista (Crass, Discharge, Rudimentari Peni, Subhumans).

podcast.title: Influence on Josh Homme
podcast.body: This hardcore punk band was particularly important to Josh Homme's development as a guitarist, with their guitarists employing a distinctive straight up and down strumming style. "two bands were particularly important, GBH and discharge. Both bands had guitarists that played with a straight up and down strumming style."

xref.title: Suicide Details (1994)
xref.body: In the early morning of Tuesday, April 5th, Kurt Cobain woke up in his bed, having slept in his clothes. He turned on MTV, found nothing interesting, then muted it to play R.E.M.'s "Automatic for the People" album. He lit a cigarette and wrote a suicide note on a legal-sized notepad, addressed to "Boddah," an imaginary friend from childhood, which he then tucked into his coat pocket. He retrieved a Remington shotgun, shells, and a cigar box full of heroin from a secret hiding place, grabbed two towels from the linen closet, and a can of Barks Root Beer from the fridge. He went to the greenhouse in the backyard, added more lines to his note, loaded three shells into the shotgun, cooked and injected $100 worth of Mexican black tar heroin into his right arm, and, before the full impact of the drug, managed to aim and pull the trigger. He likely injected so much heroin that he did not hear the gun discharge. "It began to bata. Three cigarettes later, the note was done. He stuck it in the left pocket of the code he was wearing."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Jason Everman – Paid for Bleach, Joined Nirvana, Quit, Joined Soundgarden, Quit, Became Special Forces Soldier
xref.body: Jason Everman financed the entire $606.17 recording cost of Nirvana's *Bleach* album as a favor and was falsely credited in the liner notes as having played on it. He later genuinely joined the band as second guitarist in February 1989, made his debut on February 25, 1989, and was dismissed or quit after a final show at the Pyramid Club in New York City on July 18, 1989. He subsequently joined Soundgarden as bassist, appearing on the EP *Loudest Love* (1990) and a world tour before leaving again. He then joined the US Army, served multiple tours in Afghanistan and Iraq as an elite Special Forces soldier comparable to SEAL Team 6, received an honorable discharge in 2006, enrolled in Columbia University to study philosophy, and now lives quietly in rural Washington State. "Two of the biggest grunge bands of all time, and he left both of them."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Post-Rehab Fragility and Relapse
xref.body: Upon discharge from Priory Hospital on September 8, 1994, Richie was back on the road with the band two weeks later, but remained extremely fragile, cycling between hope and hopelessness. He maintained an unhealthy regimen of smoking 65 cigarettes a day, consuming 30 cups of coffee, and drinking half a bottle of vodka daily to cope. "He was better, but still very emotionally fragile, veering from hopefulness to hopelessness. He was smoking 65 cigarettes a day and powering himself with 30 cups of coffee to counteract the half bottle of vodka he habitually drank."

xref.title: Unique Guitar Strumming Style
xref.body: Homme's distinctive guitar playing style is attributed to a combination of the straight up and down strumming techniques found in hardcore punk bands like GBH and Discharge, integrated with the strumming required for playing polkas. "You combine that with the strumming required to play polkas, and you suddenly begin to understand why Josh plays guitar the way he does, and why Queens of the Stone Age sounds just a little bit different."
